newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade gap seen at $11.8 bln in 1997--BNDES.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade gap seen at $11.8 bln in 1997--BNDES.

text.p: Brazil's trade deficit is expected to reach $11.8 billion by year-end and expand to $15.7 billion in 1998, according to a study by Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES).

The BNDES Economic Synopsis, which are based on estimates by eight investment banks and economic consultants, also forecast a balance of payments current account deficit of $33.1 billion in 1997 and $33.9 billion in 1998.
Economic growth is seen to be moderate over the next two years, with gross domestic product expected to increase 3.8 percent this year and 4.2 percent in 1998.
The Economic Synopsis estimated that the public sector deficit would amount to 3.3 percent of GDP in 1997 and decrease to 3.1 percent in 1998.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
